# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 21 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 21 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_021_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 3, Chapter 13

**1** "And the sixth mountain — the cracked one?" "The small cracks are the people who have grudges against each other and are a bit at odds — minor disputes. Many wear themselves out with this, but they can still repent and live to God. The large cracks are the chronic quarrelers — people who hold ongoing bitterness and resentment against one another. **2** These have been thrown out of the tower. It's very hard for them to repent, but if they can manage it, there's a place for them in the building. If they can't, they're done." **3** "The seventh mountain — the lush, joyful, teeming one — those are the submissive, gentle, peaceable believers. They never quarreled; they rejoiced in God's servants, wrapped themselves in the Holy Spirit, and were consistently merciful to everyone. They gave freely and without embarrassment from what they had." **4** "God sees their simplicity and their wholehearted goodness and fills them with blessing. They're worthy of eternal life — good character, genuine innocence, faithful service to God's servants." **5** "The eighth mountain — the spring-filled one where everything came to drink — those are the apostles and teachers who took the word of the Lord to the whole world with holiness and truth, who resisted evil desires and walked in righteousness and truth throughout their lives. **6** They were always at peace with each other, established in peace, and will live to God." **7** "The ninth mountain — the dangerous wilderness of beasts and serpents — those are the bad deacons: administrators who robbed widows and orphans and used their ministry for personal profit. If they stay on that path, they will die with no hope. But if they repent and serve purely going forward, there's still a chance for them." **8** "The tenth mountain — the shaded rest-place for flocks — those are the bishops and the hospitable ones who always threw open their homes to God's servants with genuine joy. These bishops never stopped sheltering the afflicted and the widows, and they lived with holiness in everything." **9** "All of these will be sheltered by the Lord forever. They are glorious in God's sight, and a place among the angels is already prepared for them — as long as they keep the Lord's commandments." **10** "The eleventh mountain — the fruit-laden one — those are the martyrs. They gave up their lives and everything they owned willingly and wholeheartedly, suffering for the name of the Lord with joy." **11** "The twelfth mountain — the pure white one — those are the innocent ones: believers who are like children, into whose hearts evil never entered. They never even knew what wickedness was. They stayed in childlike innocence all their days." **12** "These will rest with God forever, without question. And blessed are all of you who throw off wickedness and clothe yourselves in innocence — you will be the first to live to God."

---

*PNEUMA note: The final beatitude opens the twelfth-mountain ideal to everyone — innocence is not just an innate quality but something one can choose to reclaim through repentance and transformation.*
